questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have always wanted to travel to and live in Australia, and Sydney stood out because of its strong academic reputation, English-speaking environment, and unique location where the city life and beaches are closely connected. Australia offers a different academic and cultural perspective compared to Europe and Sydney in particular combines a city with easy access to nature and outdoor activities. 

The University of Technology Sydney (UTS) offered courses that aligned well with my degree, and the opportunity to experience a new education system while developing both academically and personally was an important in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, the information provided prior to arrival was clear and well structured. The application process is quite long and requires attention to detail, as there are several steps and deadlines to keep track of. However, both UCPH and UTS provided thorough and helpful information throughout the process, and there was plenty of time to complete all requirements. The host institution shared detailed guides and I received all essential information regarding enrollment, courses, and housing through emails, which made the transition to studying and living in Sydney very smooth.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Upon arrival, I received support through orientation programs and detailed information from UTS via email. The university organized welcome activities such as an introduction meeting and a campus tour, which were very helpful in getting familiar with the campus and academic environment. 

In addition, there were social events for exchange and international students, including a pub crawl, which was a fun and effective way to meet other students on exchange. Staff members and student ambassadors were available to answer questions, assist with practical matters, and provide guidance on campus facilities and student services.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was fortunate to have a friend who had been on exchange in Sydney the year before, and she was able to connect me with useful contacts. Through this network, I found the apartment I lived in. In general, finding off-campus housing in Sydney can be challenging, especially as demand is high. From what I observed and heard from other exchange students, one of the more common and effective approaches is to contact real estate agencies directly, as short-term rentals of around six months are quite common in Australia. However, it is important to note that apartments are not always furnished, so this is something future students should take into account when planning their housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living off campus. Since many universities are located in the city center and CBD area, I personally preferred living closer to the beach, especially as I only had classes on campus a few days a week. Living off campus gives you more flexibility and the opportunity to experience everyday life in Sydney. There are several very social and popular areas for exchange students, such as Bondi, where many international and exchange students choose to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was generally straightforward, although it required some planning and the completion of various forms and documents. Course registration was done through an online system where we could browse available courses and register during a designated period. I had already decided which courses I wanted in advance, which I would strongly recommend, as UTS follows a first-come, first-served principle and it is important to register quickly once the system opens.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not personally use much of the available support, as the guides and instructions provided were sufficient. However, the international student office and various online support resources were available to assist us with course selection, registration and any other questions throughout the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for my preferred courses, as I already knew which ones I wanted to apply for in advance. The system also allowed me to choose preferred days and times for my classes. If a class time was full, it was possible to join a waitlist and be enrolled if a spot became available later.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend reviewing all available courses in advance and deciding which ones you prefer before registration opens. Make sure to register as early as possible, and always have backup course options in case your first choices fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were generally comparable in level to my studies at KU, although some courses felt slightly less advanced. Overall, the academic level was appropriate and well suited for exchange students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more interactive and continuous, with regular assignments, group work and active participation throughout the semester. I really appreciated this approach, as it allowed me to work steadily with the course material and complete a significant portion of the assessment during the semester. Many courses were assessed through three to four assignments, which together made up the final grade, rather than relying solely on one final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
52703 - Media Influence
52661 - Strategic Communication in Society
52718 - The Social Life of Technology
52681 - Understanding Digital Audiences

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend Understanding Digital Audiences, as it was very relevant to my studies at home and covered similar concepts, but from a different and international perspective. The course provided valuable insights and practical understanding that complemented my academic background well.

Media Influence is also a course I would recommend, as it addresses highly relevant and contemporary topics and offers a great deal of freedom in how assignments are approached, allowing students to tailor their work to their own interests.

Strategic Communication was a more demanding course with several assignments and a strong focus on the Australian media landscape, including topics related to Indigenous issues. While this can be somewhat challenging for exchange students who are less familiar with the local context, it was still a very interesting and educational course. Overall, I was very satisfied with my course choices and found them both academically rewarding and relevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I traveled quite a lot during my exchange and was surprised by how expensive it is to travel within Australia. Australia is generally not a cheap country, so I would strongly recommend having some savings, as most students will want to explore and travel while they are there. Planning trips well in advance can help secure better prices.

I was also surprised by the high cost of renting an apartment. Housing in Sydney is significantly more expensive than in Denmark, and many students choose to share rooms in order to reduce costs. Even then, rent often ends up around 7000 - 8000 DKK per person per month. On-campus accommodation may be slightly more affordable and is worth considering.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was surprised by how expensive local transportation in Sydney was, especially buses and trains. There are no particularly student-friendly options or monthly passes, and you pay per trip, which adds up quickly. As a result, we often used Uber or DiDi, as the price was frequently similar. Food, coffee, alcohol, and eating out were roughly the same price level as in Denmark, which was less surprising and made budgeting easier than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student clubs, sports teams, beach activities, social events, trips different places in Sydney and cultural societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining student societies and sports clubs is a great way to meet people and feel integrated quickly.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Sydney’s beaches, drink coffee and go to the parks, go shopping, coastal walks, and take trips to places like the Blue Mountains or along travel a few weeks down the East Coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting was relatively easy. Australians are open, friendly and welcoming which made it easy to settle in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be active and open, join clubs, attend the social events and don’t be afraid to start conversations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The main challenges were mostly practical, such as adjusting to the cost of living and learning how to navigate a new city. It was also an adjustment to communicate exclusively in English on a daily basis, both socially and academically, and to have all courses and interactions conducted in English. However, this quickly became easier over time and was also a valuable part of the experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed lifestyle, the nice weather, outdoor culture, friendliness, and emphasis on work–life balance.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Plan ahead, especially when it comes to course registration and housing. Registration follows a first-come, first-served system, so knowing your preferred courses in advance is important.

2. Be active by joining clubs or social events early on. It makes a big difference in meeting both local and international students.

3. Make the most of the experience outside academics. Sydney and Australia have so much to offer, so take time to explore, travel and enjoy the lifestyle alongside your studies. And have the money for it :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Sydney is an amazing city to live in, but it is important to be prepared for the high cost of living. Budgeting in advance and planning trips early can help manage expenses. The academic system at UTS is more continuous than at UCPH, with several assignments throughout the semester, so staying organized from the beginning is key. 

Overall, the university provides good support for international students, and taking advantage of the resources and activities offered makes the transition much easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the growth that came from living in a completely new environment. I gained greater confidence and adaptability, while forming close friendships with people from many different countries, many of whom I will stay in touch with and bring back into my life in Copenhagen. 

Experiencing an entirely new country, culture, academic system and lifestyle in Sydney was incredibly enriching and motivating. The exchange inspired me both academically and personally, and it is an experience that I will carry with me long into the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A little challenge was studying and communicating exclusively in English every day, but it quickly became more comfortable and ultimately strengthened my academic and language skills.

questions.answer: Yes
